titleText.es: Puedes hacer esto 1 de cada 30 veces y seguir teniendo un 97% de votos positivos.
titleText.en: You can do this one in every 30 times and still have 97% positive feedback.
titleText.noteEn: The title jokes that a seller could absorb an occasional disastrous rating while keeping a high overall score.

applications.explanationEn: Qué carries a written accent because it directly asks for information.

regions.labelEs: HACER DEL MUNDO UN LUGAR MÁS EXTRAÑO. MRROWLLL

excludedUnits.rationale: This is a stylized animal vocalization rather than a Spanish lexical word.

applications.exampleEs: HACER DEL MUNDO UN LUGAR MÁS EXTRAÑO
applications.explanationEn: Hacer introduces the change, del mundo marks what is changed, and un lugar más extraño names the resulting description.

regions.labelEs: EMPEZANDO POR MI PÁGINA DE VOTOS EN EBAY.

excludedUnits.rationale: This is a commercial proper name rather than a Spanish lexical word; the surrounding Spanish feedback vocabulary carries the teachable concept.

applications.exampleEs: EMPEZANDO POR MI PÁGINA DE VOTOS EN EBAY
applications.explanationEn: Empezando presents the beginning as ongoing, por introduces the first item in the sequence, and the following words identify that starting item.

regions.labelEs: COMENTARIOS: EN LUGAR DE UNA SILLA DE OFICINA, EL PAQUETE CONTENÍA UN LINCE.

applications.explanationEn: En lugar de introduces the item that was expected as the alternative to what actually appeared.
Comprar keeps its whole dictionary form and adds -ía to express what the buyer would do.
De nuevo works as one expression meaning that the purchase would be repeated.

cards.answerEn: Write qué, cómo, cuándo, and similar words with an accent when they ask a question or add an exclamation.
cards.noteEn: This includes direct questions (¿Qué quieres?), questions inside another sentence (No sé qué quiere), and exclamations (¡Qué bonito!). Without the accent, these words usually connect parts of a sentence instead: el libro que quiero means “the book that I want.”
cards.questionEn: Why do words such as que, como, and cuando sometimes have a written accent?

cards.answerEn: to make; to turn into a new result
cards.noteEn: Hacer can describe causing a person or thing to become something new. The rest of the construction identifies what changes and the resulting role, state, or description.

example.es: La noticia hizo feliz a Marta.

cards.questionEn: How can you say that someone makes or turns a person or thing into a new result?
cards.answerEn: Use hacer, then de before the thing being changed, and then name the resulting role, state, or description.
cards.noteEn: When the thing begins with el, de + el contracts to del. Hacer changes for the person and time; the result can be a noun phrase or a description. This is a different use from ordinary hacer meaning simply ‘to do’ or ‘to make.’

example.es: La experiencia hizo de Ana una gran médica.
example.en: The experience made Ana a great doctor.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; marks what is being changed after hacer
cards.noteEn: Del combines de and el. In hacer de algo otra cosa, de introduces the thing that is made into a new role, state, or result.

example.en: They turned the garage into a workshop.

cards.noteEn: Empezando presents empezar as an action in progress. Before por, it can introduce the first item in a sequence.

example.es: Estoy empezando por la tarea corta.
example.en: I am starting with the short task.

cards.promptEs: empezar/comenzar por + primera cosa o acción
cards.questionEn: How do you identify the first item or action in a sequence?
cards.answerEn: Use a form of empezar or comenzar, then por, then the first thing or action.
cards.noteEn: The verb changes for the person and time. After por, use a noun or an unchanged action verb ending in -ar, -er, or -ir. This pattern means ‘start with’ or ‘start by.’

example.en: We will start by reviewing the data.

cards.noteEn: After empezar or comenzar, por can introduce the first thing or action in an ordered process.

cards.promptEs: valoraciones de compradores en un mercado por internet
cards.answerEn: Online marketplaces let buyers leave public ratings and written reviews about sellers and purchases.
cards.noteEn: The joke treats an absurdly dangerous shipment as one occasional bad transaction. The unhappy buyer leaves a negative review, while the title points out that many positive ratings could still hide rare disasters.
Online services may use votos for positive or negative ratings left by users, not only for votes in an election.

example.es: El producto recibió muchos votos positivos.
example.en: The product received many positive ratings.

cards.noteEn: Comentarios can label written feedback that customers leave about a purchase or seller.

example.es: Leí los comentarios de los compradores.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; begins en lugar de, ‘instead of’
cards.noteEn: Inside en lugar de, en is a fixed part of the expression rather than an independently translated location word.

example.es: Tomé té en lugar de café.
example.en: I had tea instead of coffee.

cards.noteEn: After en lugar de, use a thing or the dictionary form of an action verb. That dictionary form is called the infinitive and usually ends in -ar, -er, or -ir.
cards.questionEn: How do you say “instead of” before a thing or an action?

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; middle of en lugar de, ‘instead of’
cards.noteEn: Lugar normally means ‘place,’ but inside en lugar de the three words form one expression that introduces an alternative.

example.es: Fuimos a pie en lugar de tomar el autobús.
example.en: We walked instead of taking the bus.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; completes en lugar de, ‘instead of’
cards.noteEn: De completes en lugar de and connects it to the alternative thing or action that follows.

example.es: Usó agua en lugar de leche.
example.en: She used water instead of milk.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; links an item to its type
cards.noteEn: Spanish often uses de between an item and the noun that identifies its type. English often puts the type noun first instead: libro de historia becomes “history book.”
Contenía is a past form of contener. It often describes what something held or had inside over a stretch of past time, rather than a single momentary action.
Compraría keeps the dictionary form comprar and adds -ía. Without an explicit subject, the same form can also mean ‘he, she, or you would buy’; context identifies the person.

cards.questionEn: How do you form a Spanish “would” verb such as “would forget”?
cards.answerEn: Keep the whole dictionary form and add a conditional ending such as -ía.
cards.noteEn: The same endings attach to verbs ending in -ar, -er, and -ir. The ending changes for the person: -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, or -ían.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; begins de nuevo, ‘again’
cards.noteEn: Inside de nuevo, de is a fixed part of the expression rather than the ordinary word ‘of’ or ‘from.’

example.en: I am going to try again.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that an action happens again?
cards.answerEn: Use de nuevo after the action.
cards.noteEn: De nuevo is a common fixed expression meaning ‘again’ or ‘anew.’ Its meaning belongs to the pair, so do not translate de and nuevo separately in this use.

cards.answerEn: again; anew (as part of de nuevo)
cards.noteEn: Nuevo normally means ‘new.’ In the fixed expression de nuevo, the pair means ‘again’ or ‘anew.’
